content: 1. Escitalopram: The metabolism of escitalopram may be influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, potentially altering its levels or effects. Escitalopram can increase the toxicity of mifepristone by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Eslcarbazepine acetate: This drug may reduce the levels or effects of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. CYP3A4 inducers: The effects of CYP3A4 inducers on mifepristone have not been studied. Co-administration is not recommended by the manufacturer. 4. Estradiol: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of estradiol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Conjugated synthetic estrogens: Mifepristone may elevate the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 6. Esterified estrogens: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Estropipate: Mifepristone may elevate the levels or effects of estropipate through CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Ethinylestradiol: Mifepristone may reduce the effects of ethinylestradiol due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised, and a backup contraceptive method is recommended. 9. Etoposide: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of etoposide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 10. Etravirine: Etravirine may decrease the levels or effects of mifepristone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Fluconazole: Fluconazole may increase the levels or effects of mifepristone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Either drug may increase the toxicity of the other by prolonging the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Fentanyl: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of fentanyl by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Patients should be monitored for respiratory depression and sedation, and fentanyl dose adjustments may be required. 13. Ferrous fumarate: Mifepristone may reduce the effects of ferrous fumarate due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised, and a backup contraceptive method is recommended. 14. Flecainide: Mifepristone and flecainide may both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Alternatives should be considered if available. 15. Flibanserin: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of flibanserin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as adverse effects may increase when co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Fluticasone (inhaled): Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of inhaled fluticasone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone. 17. Formoterol: Mifepristone and formoterol may both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Alternatives should be considered if available. 18. Fosamprenavir: Either fosamprenavir or mifepristone may increase the levels of the other by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Mifepristone doses should not exceed 300 mg/day for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Gefitinib: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of gefitinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Gemifloxacin: Mifepristone and gemifloxacin may both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Alternatives should be considered if available. 21. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 22. Grapefruit: Grapefruit may increase the levels or effects of mifepristone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Haloperidol: Mifepristone and haloperidol may both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Alternatives should be considered if available. 24. Hydrocodone: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of hydrocodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 25. Ibuprofen/Famotidine: Either ibuprofen/famotidine or mifepristone may increase the toxicity of the other by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Ibutinide: Mifepristone and ibutinide may both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Alternatives should be considered if available. 27. Idelalisib: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of idelalisib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 28. Ifosfamide: Mifepristone may decrease the levels or effects of ifosfamide by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as co-administration with CYP2B6 inhibitors may reduce the therapeutic effects of ifosfamide. 29. Iloperidone: Mifepristone and iloperidone may both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Alternatives should be considered if available. 30. Imatinib: Imatinib may increase the levels or effects of mifepristone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Indinavir: Either indinavir or mifepristone may increase the levels of the other by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 32. Irinotecan: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of irinotecan by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Isradipine: Mifepristone and isradipine may both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Alternatives should be considered if available. 34. Itraconazole: Either itraconazole or mifepristone may increase the levels of the other by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Mifepristone doses should not exceed 300 mg/day for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 35. Ivacaftor: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of ivacaftor by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Ivacaftor dose reduction may be required when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 36. Ketamine: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of ketamine by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Lacosamide: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of lacosamide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 38. Lapatinib: Mifepristone may increase the levels or effects of lapatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary.
